THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 07.11.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA No.1984 of 2015  : 3 :
 2025:KER:85712  JUDGMENT (Dated this the 7th Day of November, 2025)
This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P (MV) No.60 of 2005 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Attingal.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant is that on 08.02.2002 at about 6.30 p.m, while the claimant was riding a motorcycle, another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-01-V-8450 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent, hit the claimant whereby he sustained serious injuries.
The claimant approached the Tribunal claiming a total compensation of 2,00,000/-.
3. Respondents 1 and 2 / the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle respectively, were set ex parte before the tribunal.
The 3rd respondent, insurer filed a written statement admitting the insurance policy but challenging the 2025:KER:85712 quantum of compensation claimed.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A16 were marked.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a total compensation of 25,000/- under different heads with interest @9% per annum from the date of petition till realization, against 3rd respondent being the insurer.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.

4. The award was passed finding that negligence against the respondents were not proved and awarded only an amount of 25,000/- under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short,
'the Act').
Dissatisfied with the same, the appellant has approached this Court with the above appeal.

5. On a perusal of the award it is seen that, though FIR, Scene mahazar and AMVI report of the motor cycle was 2025:KER:85712 produced as Exts.A1 to A3 respectively, the claimant failed to Abdul Saleem vs Riyasudeen on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49419562/
2 produce the final report in respect of the crime.
No evidence was adduced by the appellant to prove that there was negligence on the part of the offending motorcycle.
The tribunal found that the FIR and other connected records produced in the case was insufficient to find that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the second respondent.
Even the treatment records also did not reveal that the injury sustained to the claimant was on account of the accident.
For want of documents and evidence, the tribunal had rejected the claim for compensation under Section 166 of the Act and granted compensation under Section 140 of the Act.

When an application is filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, it is the bounden duty on the part of the claimant to prove negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle in order to claim compensation.
The 2025:KER:85712 appellant in this case has failed to prove the negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the award passed.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
